fleet.population_note: Measured over repairs that name a garage. The fleet-wide figure on the Executive dashboard also counts repairs with no garage recorded, so it is slightly different by design.

sources.method: The same fault recorded again on the same car within 90 days, credited to the garage that did the first repair. Split by how soon it came back.
sources.note: Body and rim damage are excluded — they recur because cars get scraped. Repairs from the last 90 days are excluded too: they have not had time to come back yet, and counting them as repairs that held would flatter every garage. One fault on one car on one day counts once, however many times it was labelled.

sources.method: Spans over 60 days are dropped as data-entry errors, not counted as long repairs.
NOT SCORED. The expected date equals the actual return in about 89% of rows, so an on-time rate built on it would be ~94% for every garage and would grade nobody.
sources.note: Late returns are still shown as an operational fact.

provenance.fair_comparison: Each garage is compared against what the fleet averages on the SAME mix of work it takes on, so a shop that mostly does oil services is not marked down for a fault type that recurs by schedule.
